maria (Runtime): Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we should sketch a minimal migration checklist for splitting the Dedicated GPU pool into 'strata' (reserved / shared / burst) and clearly define which admission decisions live in the operator vs the allocator.

aj (Orch): Agree. I keep thinking about the safety boundaries: operator should manage lifecycle + reserved guarantees, allocator handles per-request admission and token accounting.

sneh (SRE): Important: any change that affects prewarm/headroom must preserve emergency drain behavior. We had an incident last quarter where prewarm beans leaked capacity. :grimacing:

ryan (Infra): For infra planning we need a binding of strata -> node class. i.e. reserved => stable nodes w/ SLA, burst => spot-like nodes. That mapping must be configurable per-cluster.

maria (Runtime): Right — proposal: strata are logical labels, operator owns mapping to node pools. Allocator exposes an admission API: admit(request, strata_hint) -> (accept|queue|reject, reason). Operator exposes lifecycle control: create_stratum(name, node_selector, min_capacity, max_capacity, prewarm_policy).

pranav (Platform): Two design tradeoffs: 1) operator does aggressive eviction to protect reserved SLOs (complex to test), 2) operator is conservative and allocator performs throttles. Which do we pick?

aj (Orch): I'd pick conservative operator + richer allocator signals. Reason: operator changes are cluster-wide and slower to iterate. Keep operator simple and testable; let allocator be fast-moving.

maria (Runtime): +1. That also keeps rollback simpler. If allocator logic misbehaves we can tune admission heuristics and roll out quickly.

sneh (SRE): Tactically: add a hard-eviction kill-switch at operator level for emergencies. Also add metric: reserved_slo_violations{tenant, stratum}.

ryan (Infra): For node autoscaling we must ensure scaling signals don't thrash. Suggest: operator exposes predicted_headroom(time_window_seconds) that autoscaler consumes. Keep hysteresis in autoscaler.

pranav (Platform): Good call. Also need a cost-accounting surface: per-stratum cost ledger exported to billing. If burst gets cheap nodes we still want to attribute tokens.

maria (Runtime): Migration checklist draft (small):
- step 0: feature-flag strata label + default mapping to current pool (no behavioral change)
- step 1: operator API to define strata + node selectors (dry-run)
- step 2: allocator accepts strata_hint but falls back to legacy admission (traffic split 0/100)
- step 3: enable admission path for non-reserved strata (10% traffic)
- step 4: enable reserved enforcement with small subset of tenants (canary)
- step 5: full rollout + monitor metrics, rollback hook at each step

aj (Orch): Add explicit tests in CI to simulate node loss + prewarm loss. Also a chaos test that flips mapping of stratum -> node selector.

sneh (SRE): Observability minimums:
- per-request: admitted_stratum, admission_decision, latency, token_count
- infra: node_utilization_by_stratum, prewarm_hit_rate_by_stratum
- alerts: reserved_slo_violations, sustained_queue_growth(5m)

maria (Runtime): Sample admission API sketch (pseudo):
```
POST /allocator/v1/admit
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "model": "m-bison-7b",
  "seq_len": 2048,
  "strata_hint": "burst"
}
-> { decision: "queue", reason: "burst_pool_full", eta_seconds: 3 }
```

pranav (Platform): We need to agree semantics for strata_hint (best-effort) vs explicit pinning (hard). Pinned requests should bypass burst but consume reserved credits.

aj (Orch): Implementation note: operator should track reserved credits ledger and expose a read/write-safe RPC for allocator to subtract credits atomically. Avoid double-spend during rebalances.

ryan (Infra): On prewarming: operator exposes a prewarm API the allocator can call to request ephemeral warmed slots. Prewarm policy: max_prewarms_per_tenant and prewarm_ttl.

maria (Runtime): Rollback plan: at any step we can flip the feature flag to map all strata back to single legacy pool and switch allocator to legacy admission. Must validate no orphan prewarms.

aj (Orch): Backwards compatibility: operator should accept legacy create_pool calls and internally synthesize a default stratum named "legacy". This avoids migrating older clients.

sneh (SRE): On safety, add a canary coefficient when enabling reserved enforcement: reserved_enforce_coefficient in [0,1]. Start at 0.1 and ramp.

pranav (Platform): Testing matrix (short):
- unit: admission decisions across token sizes
- integration: operator + allocator in k8s staging cluster
- e2e: canary tenants with synthetic traffic (spike + sustained)

maria (Runtime): Open questions:
- eviction signals: should allocator suggest which running instances to preempt (by request id) or operator decide?
- multi-tenant fairness: how do we account for cached KV and prefix caching costs across strata?

aj (Orch): My vote: allocator suggests preempt candidates (ranked) and operator executes. That keeps knowledge centralized in allocator while execution stays in operator.

ryan (Infra): For prefix/KV caching, treat cached memory as "pinned" resources charged to tenant and reflected in reserved credits. We'll need tooling to surface that to tenants.

maria (Runtime): Action items:
- aj: draft operator API PR with create_stratum + mapping endpoints (due EOD Wed)
- pr: prana... sorry, @pranav: design cost-ledger schema (due Fri)
- sneh: add SLO metrics + alert playbook (due Thu)
- ry: autoscaler hysteresis proposal (due next Tue)

pranav (Platform): Will do. I'll share a sample billing export format: csv rows per minute by stratum.

orch-bot: scheduled reminder: "strata-refactor sync" in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10:00am.

maria (Runtime): Thanks all. I'll open the migration checklist doc and link PRs in this thread. :thumbsup:

aj (Orch): Nice summary. One more: add a compatibility test where a tenant specifies both strata_hint and explicit pool pinning — ensure pinning wins and is billable.

maria (Runtime): Noted. Closing loop once PRs land.

sneh (SRE): If anyone needs to run the chaos job, ping me and I'll give staging creds.

maria (Runtime): End of thread.
